instruction: To emphasize consonant sounds, please make all words that start with consonants both bold and red in color.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires making consonant-starting words both bold AND red. Verified from word list: 41 words start with consonants (do, no, say, want, now, she, was, four, so, well, get, soon, went, good, that, what, have, please, there, white, black, he, pretty, they, who, brown, ran, this, will, but, like, ride, too, with, came, must, saw, under, yes, did, new). Evaluator uses partial credit: 0.5 for bold formatting, 0.5 for red color.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for bold formatting on all consonant words, 0.5 for red color on all consonant words

llm_judge_reasons: Critical logical flaw: Metric treats each run as a single word instead of splitting by whitespace
In line 51-54, the code uses 'word = run.text.strip()' which treats entire run text as one word
If a run contains 'do no say', it will be checked as one word instead of three separate words
This will cause incorrect counting of total_consonant_words and incorrect scoring
The evaluator only checks words inside tables, which may miss words outside tables (though this appears intentional for Dolch word lists)
Postconfig correctly saves the file before verification
Color checking logic using CIEDE2000 is correct and robust
Partial credit scoring structure (0.5 bold + 0.5 color) is semantically correct
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Split run.text by whitespace to get individual words: for word in run.text.split()
Check each word separately for consonant start, bold, and color
Ensure the same run formatting (bold/color) is applied to all words extracted from that run
Example fix: Replace lines 51-64 with a loop that splits run.text and processes each word individually
